paragraph: The single-family market in North Arlington is a real seller's market. Thirty-six sales over six months at a median of $638,500, a sale-to-list ratio of 1.05, roughly 78 percent of homes closing above asking, and a median of 14.5 days on market. Buyers should expect competition on the good ones. The typical sale is a three-bedroom colonial or cape with two full baths, which is what keeps the median where it is even with sales running from $460,000 up to $1,155,000. Anchor on the median. Two-families are the other real tier here, twelve sales at a median of $820,000, all of them true two-family homes, and they move nearly as fast at 19.5 days with half closing over list. Condo and townhouse activity is essentially nonexistent, one sale in six months, so there is no tier to read there. Monthly closings are thin enough that individual months are noise, but volume built into June and July and recent medians have held in the $610,000 to $675,000 range without softening. If you're choosing between tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat, since both are competitive. It's whether you want a single-family for yourself or a two-family with rental income carrying part of the payment.
